# S213 — Release workflow hardening: changelog guard, clean notes, no stored credentials

Five hardening fixes to the proposed release workflow and its guard test: the release fails when `CHANGELOG.md` has no section for the tag, a signed tag's signature stays out of the release notes, the test and build checkouts keep no credentials, the release build does not use the Go cache, and the guards survive a reformat of the YAML. The sixth S212 later note (the BSD `getsid` helpers) is a separate E-class slice.

## Why

S212 landed the release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, 112 lines) and its text guard (`internal/release/workflow_test.go`, 135 lines). Its review left six later items, all optional hardening; this slice folds five (the owner decided on 2026-10-31 that later-notes rows fold into sweep slices and the folded rows are retired once the sweep is filed). The sixth, "freebsd vet for the getsid helpers", touches `cmd/ork` and so is E-class; it is `NEW-getsid-bsd-vet` so this slice can pair with an engine or daemon slice. Pinned action SHAs stay as they are and no action is added (S212 owner decision: checkout, setup-go, upload-artifact, download-artifact).

Re-read against HEAD of main:

- (2) No CHANGELOG section for the tag. The new-release branch builds the notes with `awk` (`.github/workflows/release.yml:107-110`); with no `## TAG` heading it prints nothing, and the release is created with only the tag message, or with an empty body for a lightweight tag. The owner writes the section before tagging (`AGENTS.md`, Release), so a missing one is a mistake: the release must fail before it is created. An existing release (`gh release view` succeeds) only gets assets and is left alone, as S212 decided.
- (3) A signed annotated tag. `git for-each-ref --format='%(contents)'` (`.github/workflows/release.yml:104`) returns the message plus the signature block. Checked on git 2.56: for a tag object whose message ends in a PGP or SSH signature block, `%(contents)` includes the block and `%(contents:signature)` is exactly that block. `%(contents:subject)` plus `%(contents:body)` would drop it but folds a multi-line first paragraph into one line, so the fix removes the `%(contents:signature)` suffix from `%(contents)`.
- (4) `actions/checkout` stores the token in `.git/config` for later steps. The test and build jobs run `go test` and `go build` only and need no git credentials (`.github/workflows/release.yml:18,44`), so they set `persist-credentials: false`. The publish job keeps the default: its `git fetch` of the tag object runs with the token (`:102`).
- (5) `actions/setup-go` caches modules and build output by default. A release build must not restore a cache that an earlier run, or a pull request, could have written, so the build job's `setup-go` sets `cache: false` (`.github/workflows/release.yml:45-47`). The test job keeps the cache; it builds nothing that ships.
- (6) The guard test matches the workflow as raw text with fixed indentation, quote style and layout (`internal/release/workflow_test.go:12-13,20,40,57,61,73,88,125-135`). A formatter pass, a 4-space indent or a quote change fails it for no real reason. The test stays stdlib-only: adding a YAML parser is a new dependency (`AGENTS.md`: ask first), and the file's own comment says "without a YAML dependency". It normalises the text first (see Implement), and the guards stay strict.

What a reformat may change, and what the guards still refuse: indentation width, quote style of the `tags` entry, comments, blank lines, trailing spaces, CRLF, and `- ` items written at the indent of their parent key. A real change (an unpinned action, a second `contents: write`, `-buildvcs=false`, a release command outside the guarded step, a dropped `persist-credentials: false`) still fails. A form the normaliser cannot read (flow-style mappings, anchors) makes the guards fail with "missing ..." rather than pass.

## Failing tests

In `internal/release/workflow_normalize_test.go`:

- TestNormalizeWorkflow (table): the real file normalises to itself; a 4-space copy normalises to the 2-space text; CRLF, trailing spaces, blank lines and comment-only lines outside a block scalar are dropped (a trailing `# v4.2.2` on a `uses:` line stays); inside a `run: |` block every line is kept, a `#` line included, with its indent relative to the block's first line unchanged; `steps:` followed by `- uses:` at the same indent comes out as `steps:` then a deeper `- uses:`; `tags: ["v*"]` and a block list `tags:` / `- 'v*'` both come out as `tags: ['v*']`; a double quote inside a `run:` line is not changed. Fails first: no `normalize`.
- TestGuardsSurviveReformatting: the full guard table passes on each of three reformatted copies of the real workflow: (a) every indent doubled to 4 spaces; (b) `tags: ["v*"]`, a comment line between every pair of steps, blank lines, trailing spaces and CRLF line ends; (c) all `- ` items at their parent key's indent. Fails first: the raw-text guards reject all three.
- TestGuardsStillFailOnRealChanges: each of these edits, made on a 4-space copy, makes the named guard fail: `actions/checkout@v4` in place of a SHA (`pinned_actions`); a `permissions:` block with `contents: write` in the build job (`permissions`); `-buildvcs=false` (`version_and_vcs`); `gh release create` moved before the guarded step (`dispatch_dry_run`); `persist-credentials: false` removed from the test job (`persist_credentials`); `cache: false` removed from the build job (`setup_go_cache`); the `END { exit !found }` line removed (`changelog_section`); `%(contents:signature)` removed (`tag_signature`).

In `internal/release/workflow_test.go` (new subtests of `TestWorkflow`, written as guards over the normalised text):

- persist_credentials: the `test` and `build` jobs each have a checkout step with `persist-credentials: false`; the `publish` job's checkout does not set it.
- setup_go_cache: the `build` job's `setup-go` step has `cache: false`, still with `go-version-file: go.mod` (the count of that string stays 2).
- changelog_section: in the guarded step, the `awk` section extraction ends with `END { exit !found }`, its failure path prints `::error::CHANGELOG.md has no section headed '## $TAG'` and exits 1, and both come before `gh release create` and after `gh release view`; the existing-release branch (`gh release upload`) is untouched.
- tag_signature: the guarded step reads `%(contents:signature)` and strips it with `${msg%"$sig"}`, and no longer redirects a bare `%(contents)` into `release-notes.md`; the tag object is still fetched before `git cat-file -t` (the existing `tag_object` guard).

## Implement

1. Write the failing tests first and run them; each must fail for the reason given.
2. `normalize(s string) string` in `workflow_normalize_test.go`, stdlib only. Steps: convert `\r\n` to `\n`; trim trailing blanks of each line; walk the lines with an indent stack. A line that ends a key with `|`, `|-`, `|+`, `>`, `>-` or `>+` starts a block scalar: its following lines that are blank or indented deeper than the key are content; keep them, shifting every line by the same amount so the first content line sits two spaces under the canonical key indent. Outside block scalars drop blank and comment-only lines; give each line the canonical indent of two spaces per stack depth; treat a line starting with `- ` at the same indent as the previous line, when that line ends with `:`, as one level deeper. Rewrite `tags:` in flow form with either quote, or as a one-item block list of `'v*'` or `"v*"`, to `tags: ['v*']`. Change nothing else, and never touch text inside a block scalar.
3. `workflow_test.go`: load the file through `normalize`; turn the `tests` table into a package-level `workflowChecks` that runs against a `reporter` interface (`Helper()`, `Errorf`, `Fatalf`) so the mutation test can run a check on a changed copy and record the failure without failing the outer test (`Fatalf` on the recorder ends the check with a panic that the runner recovers). Keep every existing assertion text-for-text unless it fails on the normalised file for a layout reason.
4. `release.yml`: add `with:` / `persist-credentials: false` to the checkouts of the `test` and `build` jobs; add `cache: false` under the build job's `setup-go` `with:`. In the guarded step's `else` branch: fetch the tag (unchanged), then
   `awk ... END { exit !found } ... CHANGELOG.md > changelog-section.md` inside `if ! ...; then echo "::error::CHANGELOG.md has no section headed '## $TAG'"; exit 1; fi`, then the annotated-tag test, then `msg=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(contents)' ...)`, `sig=$(git for-each-ref --format='%(contents:signature)' ...)`, `printf '%s\n\n' "${msg%"$sig"}" > release-notes.md`, then `cat changelog-section.md >> release-notes.md`, then `gh release create` as before. Do not change any `uses:` line or its SHA; do not add an action, a job, or a secret.
5. `AGENTS.md` Release section: add two sentences (the release fails without a CHANGELOG section for the tag; a signed tag's signature is left out). Mark as *proposed* like the rest of the section.
6. `CHANGELOG.md`, last (so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict): one entry at the top of `## Unreleased`, marked *proposed*, listing the five changes.
7. Do not touch: `cmd/ork`, any Go file outside `internal/release`, the existing-release branch, the pinned SHAs, the `permissions` blocks. The workflow cannot run in the worktree and must not be pushed or dispatched from it.
